## Abstract

Cell--cell communication (CCC) coordinates cellular activities that vary dynamically across biological contexts.
Most computational tools infer CCC by aggregating cells into predefined types, obscuring the single-cell heterogeneity that distinguishes functional subpopulations; conversely, methods that preserve single-cell resolution disregard how communication is differentially regulated across multiple conditions.
To bridge this gap, we developed CCC-RISE, an extension of the tensor-based method Reduction and Insight in Single-cell Exploration (RISE).
Rather than relying on cell-type labels, CCC-RISE uses PARAFAC2-derived eigen-states to deconvolve communication into interpretable programs defined by conditions, sender cells, receiver cells, and ligand--receptor pairs, then maps each program back to the individual cells involved.
Applied to lung transplant and Crohn's disease cohorts, CCC-RISE identified transcriptionally distinct sender and receiver subpopulations beyond available cell-type labels, revealed coordinated signaling mediated by immune proteins that was associated with disease outcome, and characterized a transitional spectrum of cells between hormone-secreting states.
Label-based tensor methods split, missed, or assigned these programs to whole cell types.
CCC-RISE thus resolves disease-relevant signaling subpopulations invisible to aggregate methods by analyzing multi-condition data while preserving single-cell resolution.

**Highlights**

- CCC-RISE analyzes cell--cell communication across conditions at single-cell resolution, without relying on predefined cell-type labels

- It deconvolves communication into interpretable programs defined by conditions, sender cells, receiver cells, and ligand--receptor pairs

- Mapping programs back to individual cells reveals mutually exclusive signaling subpopulations whose granularity exceeds that of available annotations

- In a lung transplant cohort, CCC-RISE identifies a coordinated communication axis associated with allograft function and patient survival

## Data availability

- The ALAD single-cell gene expression, cell-type annotations, and clinical annotations were obtained from Calabrese et al.\ [@doi:10.1016/j.healun.2024.02.007].

- The IBD single-cell gene expression, cell-type annotations, and biopsy metadata were obtained from Array Express E-MTAB-16986 (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/biostudies/arrayexpress/studies/E-MTAB-16986)\ [@ibdverse-arrayexpress; @doi:10.1038/s41588-026-02634-7].

- Scripts to reproduce the manuscript are available on GitHub (https://github.com/meyer-lab/cccRISE).
